source.title: Reward revaluation biases hippocampal replay content away from the preferred outcome.
authors: Matthijs A A van der Meer

confidence_rationale: The principled counterweight. Rats shifted behaviour TOWARD a restricted outcome but replay content shifted AWAY from it -- replay prioritization is NOT a simple reward-magnitude or behavioural-preference proportionality. Supports MECH-443's core (replay content is prioritized by motivational state, not recent experience) while refuting the naive shape of the priority function -- which is exactly the refinement the registration must encode (priority = update-utility/need, not reward level). Direct recordings, clean revaluation design.
failure_signatures: Replay content moved AWAY from the currently most-valuable outcome, falsifying any MECH-443 implementation that equates priority with reward magnitude or current behavioural preference.
The dissociation between behaviour (toward restricted outcome) and replay (away from it) means a REE priority signal read off the action-value of the committed policy would point the wrong way.

mapping.source_claim_statement: After motivational revaluation (hunger/thirst shifts), rats behaviourally favoured the restricted outcome, yet awake replay content was biased AWAY from that outcome and toward the non-restricted one; replay content is not limited to recent experience or trajectories toward the preferred goal.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-443: confirms replay is prioritized by internal/motivational state rather than recent experience (supports a non-uniform, state-conditioned write channel) BUT refutes the naive priority = reward-magnitude reading -- the priority must be an update-utility/need signal (cover under-sampled or to-be-needed states), consistent with Mattar & Daw's gain x need, not reward level. MECH-444: a target refreshed against 'current value' would mis-prioritize here; the relevant signal is need/coverage, not current preferred-outcome value.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is awake replay on a spatial T-maze under hunger/thirst revaluation; the away-from-preferred direction may be specific to coverage/exploration demands of that task and need not generalize to every prioritization regime, but it decisively rules out reward-magnitude as THE priority variable.
mapping.source_context: Rodent hippocampal recordings; T-maze free choice between food and water under alternating hunger/thirst restriction.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality; counted as mixed because it both confirms state-conditioned prioritization and refutes the simplest priority function -- the most decision-relevant paper for how to SHAPE the MECH-443 signal.
